response.sql: WITH per_name AS (SELECT e.event_name AS event_name, AVG(b.amount) AS avg_amount FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE b.amount IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.event_name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS overall_avg FROM per_name) SELECT p.event_name, p.avg_amount, p.avg_amount - o.overall_avg AS diff_from_overall, p.avg_amount / o.overall_avg AS ratio_to_overall FROM per_name p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_amount > o.overall_avg;

assumptions.assumption: Budget lines are matched to events by budget.link_to_event = event.event_id, and the inner join drops budget lines with no matching event.

Budget lines with a NULL amount are excluded before averaging; the overall average is the unweighted mean of the per-event-name averages, computed over all names before the above-average filter is applied.
Event names are grouped exactly as stored (case and whitespace sensitive). Events with a NULL event_name form one shared group, which is counted as a name in the overall average.

alternatives.interpretation: Same computation, but events with a NULL event_name are excluded entirely, so they do not form a group or count toward the overall average.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_name AS (SELECT e.event_name AS event_name, AVG(b.amount) AS avg_amount FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE b.amount IS NOT NULL AND e.event_name IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.event_name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS overall_avg FROM per_name) SELECT p.event_name, p.avg_amount, p.avg_amount - o.overall_avg AS diff_from_overall, p.avg_amount / o.overall_avg AS ratio_to_overall FROM per_name p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_amount > o.overall_avg;
